principles: Fill the minimal evidence-supported frontier before completing non-binding nodes.
A headroom ratio is admitted only when capacity and requirement share unit, scope and time basis and the requirement is independent of the capacity model.
Observed, modeled and derived measurements remain distinct; price/lead-time signals establish scarcity direction but are not quantity headroom.
Do not use a generation interconnection queue as a load interconnection denominator or a regional request queue as national realized demand.
Preserve UNKNOWN and specify the next observation that could close it rather than manufacturing a precise ratio.

A customer-specific independent demand lower bound can narrow an endogenous-denominator gap without becoming total market demand; configuration and product scope must still match before headroom admission.

evidence.claimBoundary: 2026 Huawei production/memory mix model. Median 1.5M Ascend units, 0.88M H100e; domestic CXMT/XMC HBM supports about 240k 950DT 96GB units. Model outputs and assumptions, not provider shipment truth.
Epoch input sheet: CXMT 2026 year-end HBM exit rate 30k WSPM median (22-40k), FE yield 35% (25-45%), 8-hi backend yield 70% (55-82%), five-month lead, and XMC 3k WSPM modeled assumption.

Huawei 2026 Ascend 950 architecture whitepaper lists 950DT memory variants 144GB/96GB with 4TB/s bandwidth and 950PR 128GB/112GB with 1.6/1.4TB/s. Product specifications are vendor-owned, not independent performance validation.

Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu says the company cannot produce enough AI computing equipment to satisfy China demand and therefore does not plan full-scale international expansion. Directional excess-demand evidence; no quantity.

Reports HBM shortage and export controls raising Chinese AI accelerator costs; Huawei 950DT indicated price >250k yuan, 20-50% above quotes two months earlier. Price is a scarcity signal, not quantity headroom.
Reports selected U.S. high-voltage transformer lead times up to 160 weeks and multi-year advance procurement. Lead time is direct schedule pressure, not a capacity/requirement ratio.

DOE identifies transformer supply-chain vulnerability; distribution-transformer lead times rose from 3-6 months in 2019 to 12-30 months in 2023 latest available on that page. Different class/time from high-voltage transformers.
Berkeley Lab reports >2,060GW generation+storage seeking U.S. transmission interconnection at end-2025. Dataset explicitly concerns generation/storage requests, not load interconnection demand.

Berkeley Lab 2026 Speed to Power documents bottlenecks slowing large-load connections and more than 40 solution classes. Establishes a load-side process problem but does not provide one national load-queue MW denominator.

ERCOT June 18 2026 says it was tracking more than 438,000MW of large-load requests, nearly 89% data centers. Requested load is not approved or energized capacity and is ERCOT-regional, not U.S.-national.

ERCOT March 2026 TAC report provides a project-status funnel for loads associated with 2026: 5,768MW observed energized, 2,759MW approved to energize but not operational, 3,181MW planning studies approved, 7,353MW under review, 2,704MW no studies submitted, total 21,765MW. This is a dated ERCOT regional project-status view, not national load demand or deliverable grid headroom.

Bloomberg reports DeepSeek plans to deploy at least 160,000 Huawei top accelerators (Ascend 950DT in the report) at an Inner Mongolia data center. This is an independently sourced customer demand lower bound/plan, not a Huawei shipment, fulfilled order, or China-wide demand census.

National Laboratory of the Rockies January 2026 supply summary for U.S. LPTs >=100 MVA: domestic production model roughly 325-700 units in 2025-2026 and imports 500-700/year, yielding 825-1,400 total annual availability in 2025; planned expansions reflected in later years. Modeled availability, not committed deliveries.

NLR 2026 planning study translates National Transmission Planning Study scenarios into 2025-2035 component requirements. Across transformer categories, AC requires 15,094 units / 1,510 per year average; MT requires 13,713 / 1,370 per year average. The study assumes large power transformers >=100 MVA. Scenario-average planning requirement, not current order backlog.

FERC June 18 2026 issued large-load interconnection show-cause orders to six jurisdictional RTOs/ISOs, evidence that load interconnection process/readiness is a distinct regulatory/operational object. This action is not a national MW demand denominator.

POWER summarizes Wood Mackenzie 2025 market research estimating about a 30% U.S. power-transformer shortfall, with high-voltage/GSU classes especially stressed. This is a market-model estimate from a secondary publication and uses a broader product framing than NLR >=100MVA planning components; retained as structured challenge evidence, not merged mechanically with NLR ratios.

SJ Semiconductor IPO review response reports chiplet/multi-chip integration packaging capacity utilization of 71.85% in 2023, 57.62% in 2024, and 63.42% in 2025H1. Historical utilization, not a 2026 current-capacity observation.

Mirror of SJ Semiconductor 2026H1 report: chiplet/multi-chip packaging revenue grew 2.61% YoY and represented 53.66% of revenue; company states core material supply for chiplet/multi-chip packaging remained tight and reports ongoing 2.5D/3DIC technology and capacity expansion. Does not disclose current 2.5D utilization.

SK hynix Q2 2026 results state customer demand exceeds supply capabilities, HBM4 mass shipments began in Q2 and ramp in H2, and long-term agreements with around 10 key customers are in place. Global supplier condition, not U.S.-specific allocation.
Samsung Q2 2026 results expect server/HBM demand growth and continued supply constraints despite production increases. Global supplier statement, not U.S.-specific allocation.
TrendForce estimates HBM wafer input among top three DRAM suppliers reaches ~22% of total DRAM wafer input at end-2026; global production-allocation metric, not U.S. HBM supply.

TrendForce estimates overall DRAM sufficiency ratio about -1% to -2% in 2026 and says HBM allocation contributes to tight supply. Overall DRAM balance is contextual evidence only; it is not HBM-specific headroom.

TrendForce Sep 29 2026 says HBM supply remains tight into 2027, with limited supply and yield/ramp time contributing to higher price outlook. Current global scarcity direction; no U.S.-specific quantity.

TrendForce News, citing Economic Daily/institutional estimates, reports CoWoS supply-demand gap around 20% mid-2026 narrowing toward 10% by year-end, with TSMC monthly CoWoS capacity estimated 120k-140k wafers and OSAT partners 50k-60k. Secondary quantified estimate, not TSMC capacity disclosure and not U.S.-domestic capacity.
TrendForce reports persistent CoWoS/2.5D shortage in 2026 and expects severe global 2.5D packaging shortage to begin easing in 2027 as capacity expands. Global complement condition.

CBRE H1 2026 primary North American markets: 10,903MW supply, 1.4% vacancy, 7,481.1MW under construction, 80.4% preleased; market scope covers eight primary North American markets and is not AI-only energized IT capacity.

JLL midyear 2026 broader North America scope reports ~1% vacancy, >66GW under construction and 95% pre-committed. Broader market definition than CBRE; not directly mergeable with CBRE primary-market figures.
EIA reports 86GW planned U.S. utility-scale capacity additions in 2026 and 53GW realized additions in 2025. Nameplate additions are not firm site-level deliverability.

EIA February-STEO-based analysis forecasts U.S. electricity load +1.9% in 2026 and +2.5% in 2027, with much faster ERCOT/PJM regional growth; modeled analysis says most regions can accommodate higher-than-expected demand under fixed capacity assumptions, while ERCOT shows stronger stress. National load/generation context, not site headroom.

2026 China Computing Power Conference report states 15.56 million standard racks in use and 2,185 EFLOPS FP16 intelligent compute as of June 2026. Aggregate compute/rack measures are not high-density AI-ready energized IT headroom.

China NEA reports internet data services consumed 695 hundred-million kWh (69.5 TWh) Jan-Aug 2026, +42.5% YoY; category is broader than AI data centers. August alone 102 hundred-million kWh, +37.9% YoY.
China NEA reports 4.08TW installed generation capacity at end-July 2026, +11.0% YoY, and about 194GW new generation capacity Jan-Jul. Nameplate capacity is not firm AI-site deliverability.
China NEA reports national peak load reached a record 1.56TW in August 2026, about 49.69GW above prior-year maximum, while the system served repeated high-load days. Peak system load is not AI load.

People.cn industry reporting states China transformer exports reached CNY39.792B in 2026H1, +26.78% YoY; exports of >10MVA liquid transformers grew >50%. Export value/growth indicate manufacturing scale and external demand, not domestic spare capacity.

Digital China portal republishes CCTV reporting that many Guangdong/Jiangsu transformer factories were at full production and some data-center transformer orders extended to 2027. Qualitative industry sample, not a national matched MVA backlog series.

China NEA reports 46 UHV corridors operating in summer 2026 and west-to-east transfer capability above 340GW, while the system handled repeated record/high-temperature loads. National transfer capability does not establish local AI-site connection headroom.
